title: ESA FIDUCIAL REFERENCE MEASUREMENT (FRM) ATLAS - EXPRO+
description: The ESA Fiducial Reference Measurement (FRM) Atlas is an Earth Observation initiative led by to develop an open-access platform forFRM and calibration/validationknowledge.FRMs are fully characterised, traceable measurements with documented uncertainties, used to assess the accuracy and quality of satellite products.ESA-supported FRM activities cover domains including ocean colour, altimetry, surface temperature, atmospheric composition, vegetation, soil moisture and radar.As their associated datasets, procedures and expertise are distributed across many platforms, a centralised mechanism is needed to improve accessibility and interoperability.TheAtlas will provide a single entry point for discovering FRM projects, datasets, procedures, campaigns, documentation, infrastructures and experts.It will connect FRMs with satellite missions, products, variables and validation methodologies,while federating existing resources rather than duplicating them.Its objectives are to improve discoverability, support best practices, promote knowledge reuse and harmonisation, and maximise the value of ESA's Cal/Val investments.

title: STUDY OF CELL-BIOLOGICAL MECHANISMS OF AUTOPHAGY DEVELOPMENT UNDER MICROGRAVITY CONDITIONS FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF TECHNOLOGIES FOR PRODUCING ESTABLISHED PLANT PRODUCTS ON SPACE PLATFORMS - EXPRO PLUS
description: Plants are expected to contribute to future exploration systems by providing food, biological resources and regenerative functions during long-duration missions. However, altered-gravity environments can affect plant growth, development, intracellular transport, stress signalling and resource allocation. Autophagy and programmed cell death are conserved cellular processes involved in the degradation and recycling of cellular components and in the regulation of plant development and stress adaptation. Their interaction with cytoskeletal organisation and metabolic regulation may therefore influence the capacity of plants to maintain stable growth and productivity under space-relevant conditions. The objective of the activity is to improve understanding of the cellular and molecular mechanisms that govern plant adaptation to altered-gravity conditions and to translate this knowledge into recommendations supporting reliable plant-based biological production on future space platforms.

title: PORTABLE SELF-CALIBRATED RYDBERG ELECTRIC FIELD PROBE FOR ANTENNA MEASUREMENTS - EXPRO+
description: Objective:To design and realize a first European portable self-calibrated SI-traceable Rydberg atom-based Electric field probe.Description:Accurate measurement of electric fields is crucial for the development and operation of RF communicationsystems, particularly in space missions. Conventional antennas need fine calibration for high-integrity reception. The calibration is performed by placing uncalibrated antennas in a known EM (electromagnetic) environment that is measured via a well-calibrated antenna which creates a dependency. Whereas Rydberg based receivers allow precise measurements of RF signals which is directly related to Planck's constant and hence can self-calibrate by relying on SI (international system of units)-traceable atomic standards The activity aims to develop a portable, self-calibrated Rydberg atom based electric field probe.The probe is based on the interaction of RF-fields with Rydberg atoms, where alkali atoms are excited opticallyto Rydberg states and the applied RF-field alters the resonant state of the atoms. For this probe, the Rydbergatoms are placed in a glass vapor cell. The vapor cell acts like an RF-to-optical transducer, converting an RF Efield to an optical frequency response. The probe utilizes the concept of Electromagnetic Induced Transition (EIT), where the RF transition in the four-level atomic system causes a split of the transition spectrum for the pump laser. This splitting is measured and is directly proportional to the applied RF field amplitude. Therefore, by measuring this splitting, we get a direct measurement of the RF E-field strength. This technique could allow traceable measurements over a large frequency band including 1-500GHz. The new approach has the following benefits: 1) it will allow direct SI units linked RF E-field measurements, 2) It is self-calibrating due to atomic resonances, 3) it will provide RF field measurements independent of current techniques, 4) the probe will not perturb the field during the measurement, since no metal is present in the probe.This activity encompasses the following tasks:-Assessment of different Rydberg atom-based methods of detection of RF fields.- Requirement consolidation and performance assessment.- Detailed concept design with analysis of critical functions.- Development of the breadboard and verification in relevant environment.- Development of a technology roadmap for an EQM.

title: AI-AUGMENTED HAZARD DETECTION AND AVOIDANCE FOR THE L4 ENCELADUS LANDER - EXPRO+
description: ObjectivesAssess the feasibility of using physics-based granular dynamics simulation to model the formation of cryovolcanic terrains on Enceladus and derive insights into surface compactness. Develop a proof-of-concept ML model for inferring snow/ice geophysicalproperties (e.g., density, snow water equivalent) by correlating terrestrial in-situ scientific data with satellite remote sensing observations. Initiate the adaptation of classical, optimization-based HDA frameworks to integrate AIderived geophysical safety maps, establishing a baseline for a future hybrid HDA architecture. Conduct an extensive performance and resource consumption benchmark of key AI and HDA software components on representative space-grade hardware, establishing the trade-space between algorithmic capability and on-board computational budgetDescriptionThe ESA Voyage 2050 L4 mission to Enceladus requires an autonomous landing in the South Polar Terrain to achieve its core astrobiological objectives. This environment presents unique challenges that transcend classical HDA capabilities. Landing hazardsare not only geometric (e.g., slopes, rocks), but also geophysical. Due to the unknown load-bearing capacity of cryovolcanic surface deposits, landing sites can appear perfectly flat and clear of hazards and yet be catastrophically unsafe. Classical existing Hazard Detection and Avoidance (HDA) frameworks targeting Moon and Mars, are highly mature for geometric hazard assessment but are not designed to infer subsurface geophysical properties from remote sensing data. This activity shall address this critical technology gap by investigating the integration of AI/ML-based geophysicalinference into a proven HDA decision-making architecture. Additionally, the severe power and computational constraints of a solar-powered missionto Saturn imposea hard limit on the complexity of on-board AI. It is currently unknown what level of "intelligence" is achievable within a realistic resource budget. This activity shall perform the foundational trade-off analysis required to inform mission designers of the necessary hardware and power provisions for a reliable and capable AI-augmented HDA system

title: MATURATION OF ZERO BOIL OFF COMPONENTS (RTB CRYOCOOLER) OF LIQUID OXYGEN (LOX) - EXPRO+
description: Objective:  To design and develop a cryocooler breadboard model, based on the Reverse Turbo-Brayton, targeting LOx temperature, for the long duration storage of liquid cryogenic propellants for in Space application. Description:  Cryogenic propellants are being considered and baselined for future missions as a valid alternative to storable propellants for orbital and deep space missions.A combination of Liquid Oxygen (LOX) and Liquid cryogenic propellants provide significant advantages in term of performance over storable fuel and oxidizers.  Several classes of orbital and deep space missions can benefit from cryogenic propulsion systems. However, cryogenic propulsion systems technologies are only available for short duration missions (max. 1 day, launchers). Extending the operating life of these systems requires a range of new technologies, more adapted to high volume transfer at lower pressure, andfor a long-time duration of operations and long cycles in space (days to weeks).  Handling cryogenic fluid in space for long duration necessitates the introduction of a so called Zero Boil off systems where active cooling systems are needed.  In order to increase TRL for such system and especially for the cryocooler part, this activity targets to design, manufacture a testing model and perform test under representative environment on ground, targeting the LOx temperature range, of around 90K, coinciding also with sub-cooled LCH4, and would also demonstrate the first technological bricks for a LH2 RTB cryocooler of such size. Also the heat lifts is targeted to be in the range of 100-200W, which is considered an important stepping stone into enabling zero boil-off components storage in-orbit of cryogenic propellants.   This activity encompasses the following tasks:   - - - - Requirements definition, design trade-offs, a development plan, industrial plan (incl. make or buy analyses) to reach TRL4 at the end of the activity at component level, A systems sizing exercise (considering ZBO LOX tank application), and the associated detailed design of the 90K Class RTB Breadboard Test plan, HW manufacturing and testing Test results exploitation, lessons learned and recommendations for future or complementary development Deliverables: Breadboard, Report
